text: When I think back on my journey with FromSoftware games, it feels almost surreal how it all started and how it eventually led me to Elden Ring. My very first step into the world of soulslike games was not through the most traditional door. It was 2023, I still had my PlayStation 4, and instead of starting with Dark Souls or Bloodborne like most people recommend, I chose Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. Looking back, it was a strange, almost reckless choice for a beginner. Sekiro is unforgiving, precise, and merciless. For six long months I struggled, died countless times, cursed my own hands, and questioned if I would ever finish it. But eventually, after endless hours of practice and persistence, I overcame the final boss and realized something life-changing: I wasn’t just playing a game, I was experiencing something deeper, something that demanded every bit of me. And I fell in love.  From that moment, it was impossible to stop. I dived headfirst into the entire Dark Souls trilogy, one after another, discovering the haunting beauty, the cryptic lore, and the brutal yet rewarding gameplay loop that defines these worlds. Each death taught me patience, every victory felt like a triumph carved in stone. It was a cycle of despair and euphoria that I couldn’t resist. And then came Bloodborne, the crown jewel for me personally. Fast, aggressive, atmospheric in a way that no other game has matched—Bloodborne became my absolute favorite, the one that still lingers in the back of my mind long after I put down the controller.  I thought I had seen the peak of what FromSoftware could offer, until I decided to try Elden Ring. At first, I picked it up again on my old PS4, still buzzing from my past journeys. The game’s world was vast and breathtaking, yet I couldn’t ignore the painful reality: its performance was terrible on that console. Stuttering framerates, muddy textures, and constant slowdowns turned what should have been a magical experience into a frustrating one. I gave up after thirteen hours, not because the game lacked brilliance, but because I couldn’t bear to see it run that poorly. For a time, Elden Ring remained a distant dream, something I respected but couldn’t fully embrace.  That changed this year. After months of saving, I finally built my own gaming PC, capable of handling almost everything at over 90 to 100 FPS. The very first game I knew I had to buy again was Elden Ring. And the moment I stepped back into the Lands Between, it was like rediscovering the magic of FromSoftware all over again. The sheer scale of the open world, the haunting beauty of its landscapes, the freedom to carve my own path—it all felt overwhelming in the best way possible. Every detail amazed me, from the subtle environmental storytelling to the sheer brutality of its enemies. Combat felt smoother than ever, bosses were terrifying and awe-inspiring, and exploration never ceased to surprise me. Elden Ring isn’t just a game—it’s an odyssey, an entire world begging to be uncovered layer by layer.  And yet, despite all that, I still feel like I’ve only scratched the surface. Even after completing my first playthrough and diving into New Game+, I know there are still secrets hidden away, builds I’ve yet to experiment with, and corners of the world I haven’t truly explored. That’s why, for now, I haven’t bought the DLC. Not because I don’t want to, but because I believe I haven’t yet absorbed everything Elden Ring already has to offer me. One day I’ll get there, and when I do, I know I’ll savor every second of that new chapter.  Until then, Elden Ring remains not just another game in my library, but a monumental experience—one that continues to remind me why I fell in love with soulslikes in the first place. And when the time comes to step into its DLC, I know I’ll cherish every moment as if it were the very first time.

text: Back in 2011 my friend got me to play Dark Souls. I loathed it. I had no comprehension of the game's stats, general level layout, or mechanics. I let myself be lead around by the nose and more or less gifted an electric zweihänder that I could barely lift to carry me along.  Fast forward to 2022, this new Elden Ring game is being lauded as the greatest thing since sliced bread. And I was skeptical. It wasn't until a coworker, a silly man in his late 50s proudly declared that he was 'the Elden Lord', if he could beat it so could I. So I bought the game.  I decided I wanted a faith/strength build as I quite adore the paladin archetype. So I picked that class- But I could not understand in the slightest what I was doing. I ran along and somehow ended up in Liurnia before I'd even seen a boss. One lobster chase later I was ready to put the game down and get back my money.  Then my friend stepped in. He gave me simple instructions; "Pick wretch so that you are introduced to the game's mechanics slowly over time. Then, pick any direction and follow it in a straight line and see where your adventure takes you- It is after all an open world game."  So I made a wretch, with literally nothing to lose but my precious loincloth and stick. I settled on my first objective, *find pants*. And so I left in a straight line heading east by north-east. I entered Caelid. Right at the gates I was greeted by the invader, Anastasia. I understood her move-set instantly, she was Maneater Mildred all-over. She killed me, several times. But in the end I got her- And I felt accomplished. I traveled further into Caelid and eventually came upon a merchant who sold me pants. There after I entered a divine tower and ran into a black flame cultist who flattened me.  A bit flummoxed I returned to my friend. "You're certainly in the wrong area, return to the tutorial area and head due south.", he said. There I met Gronk the Magic Potato Dog- but I digress. I kept to this pattern, pick a direction and see what I find. Found my favorite weapon in the game, the iron cleaver, and thereafter I came to enjoy my goofy clueless romps across the Lands Between. I got into a pattern of never keeping runes on me- they would go to waste as I wasn't any good.  And I kept at this, and eventually I beat the game. Then I beat it again, and again. Until I'd had all the achievements. I learned mechanics, that if you encounter an obstacle it can be overcome with just a bit of wit and preparation. And throughout I was joyful for Anastasia numerous returns.  Though.... As someone who went through Mohg's fight twice without either macguffin I can say clearly, fuck Mohg.

But in the end I got her- And I felt accomplished. I traveled further into Caelid and eventually came upon a merchant who sold me pants. There after I entered a divine tower and ran into a black flame cultist who flattened me.  A bit flummoxed I returned to my friend. "You're certainly in the wrong area, return to the tutorial area and head due south.", he said. There I met Gronk the Magic Potato Dog- but I digress. I kept to this pattern, pick a direction and see what I find. Found my favorite weapon in the game, the iron cleaver, and thereafter I came to enjoy my goofy clueless romps across the Lands Between. I got into a pattern of never keeping runes on me- they would go to waste as I wasn't any good.  And I kept at this, and eventually I beat the game. Then I beat it again, and again. Until I'd had all the achievements. I learned mechanics, that if you encounter an obstacle it can be overcome with just a bit of wit and preparation. And throughout I was joyful for Anastasia numerous returns.  Though.... As someone who went through Mohg's fight twice without either macguffin I can say clearly, fuck Mohg.

text: First of all, the first gameplay experience is unmatched. The world is insanely beautiful, the characters are memorable, and the voice acting is perfect. Every line feels heavy and meaningful. The dialogues hit hard...you can feel the weight behind them.  About the Difficulty :  The game’s difficulty depends entirely on how you choose to play. Yes, skill matters...but even a noob like me can finish this game.  If you decide to fight bosses without summons or without some broken one-shot build, the game becomes hard as hell. You’re forced to rely purely on skill. Summons, on the other hand, make the game much easier.  For me, Mimic Tear carried my entire playthrough, even against Malenia, and I was using a pretty random build to be honest. For some reason, Mimic Tear didn’t help much in the Radagon fight...but Tiche absolutely did.  I personally don’t want to spend hours fighting a single boss. My first playthrough took 94 hours, and even with Mimic Tear helping me, it already took a long time. Without Mimic Tear, it would’ve taken me way more than that...there’s honestly no way I could’ve completed the game. That said, there is one thing that genuinely made the game harder for me...and I’ll explain that in the “What I Hate” section.  What I Loved About the Game :  The beautiful environment goes without saying, but exploration is the real star of Elden Ring.  This is the only game where I explored this much. I’ve never explored any other game the way I explored this one...not even Red Dead Redemption 2 or The Witcher 3, where exploration is also a huge focus. Everywhere you go, something is waiting for you...a boss, a weapon, a Somber Smithing Stone, or even something you didn’t know you needed.  Even when I found items I wasn’t interested in, it still felt satisfying. Exploration never felt wasted. Even after exploring for hours, I still feel like there are so many things left to discover.  Honestly, 60–70% of my playtime was just exploration, not boss fights ...and I loved every second of it.  One more thing I absolutely loved was weapons, especially my favorite one.. the Uchigatana with the Unsheathe skill. I honestly can’t explain how satisfying that weapon feels. I used the Uchigatana for almost every boss in the game, right up until I found Rivers of Blood. The Unsheathe skill just hits different.  I know the Uchigatana isn’t really a late-game weapon...at least not with the skillset I have...but it’s still my favorite weapon in the game, no lie.  As for the story… I’ll be honest I barely understood anything except “Put these foolish ambitions to rest.” I’ll definitely watch lore videos later. I’m just bad at grasping stories when the narration isn’t direct. But I’m sure it won’t disappoint.  Boss designs and movesets are also fantastic.  What I Hated About the Game :  This is purely my opinion nd you don’t have to agree.  The combat. I don’t enjoy dodging 3–4 attacks just to land one hit or only to get interrupted or staggered while using a skill attack. Many weapons have amazing movesets, but the real question is ...can we actually use them effectively? I’m not so sure. Maybe skill issue from my side ..but srsly.  Another thing I hated was how the dodge  works.  Dodging doesn’t always respond instantly if you’re already attacking or stuck at the end of an animation and that often gets you hit. My first Soulslike game was Black Myth Wukong, where dodging is instant. No matter what you’re doing...if you press dodge, you dodge.  That’s why combat in BMW feels so much better and more satisfying to me than in Elden Ring.  That’s exactly how I wanted Elden Ring’s dodge to feel. If dodging worked like that, half the game would instantly feel easier. And that’s why BMW felt much easier to me compared to Elden Ring. If instant dodge were removed from BMW, it wouldn’t be any easier than Elden Ring at all.  This is honestly the only major thing I hated about the game.  Final Verdict :  Despite my complaints, I absolutely loved exploring this world, and overall, I enjoyed the game a lot.  I’ll still say it straight: Elden Ring is a 10/10. You won’t regret buying this game and giving it a shot.
